skill.name: revdoku

skill.summary: Publish reviewed static websites and files with Revdoku.
skill.author: revdoku

security_audit.summary: The skill is a static-site publishing CLI with legitimate network, filesystem, and credential operations; most pattern matches are benign documentation, exclusions, or quoted shell usage. Publication is not recommended without remediation because the documented installer executes unverified remote code, and the CLI has credential and repository-binding trust-boundary weaknesses. Static review was capped at 400/670 representative findings; omitted static matches are unconfirmed, so automatic publishing stays disabled until manual review.

remediation.suggestion: Manually review the omitted 270 static analyzer matches or reduce bundled generated/vendor/reference content before enabling automatic publication.

remediation.issue: Remote installer execution is not integrity-verified.
remediation.suggestion: Publish versioned release artifacts with pinned SHA-256 hashes or signatures, verify them before execution, and replace curl-to-bash instructions with a reviewed download-and-verify flow.

remediation.issue: A configurable base URL can receive the saved Bearer token.
remediation.suggestion: Restrict authenticated requests to an allowlist of trusted HTTPS origins, require explicit confirmation for a changed origin, and use separate credentials for self-hosted deployments.

remediation.issue: A repository-controlled .revdoku binding can select a target bucket for destructive publishing.
remediation.suggestion: Show the resolved bucket and deletion scope, then require explicit confirmation before publish when a binding file is first encountered or changes.

remediation.issue: An existing credentials file can retain permissive permissions.
remediation.suggestion: Explicitly set owner-only permissions after every credentials-file write and reject credential files with insecure ownership or mode.

semantic_findings.title: Unverified remote bootstrap execution
semantic_findings.description: The installer downloads the Revdoku executable and marks it executable without verifying a signature or checksum. The documentation also directs users to execute a remotely fetched installer through bash.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The script download and executable permission change are direct, and no integrity verification is present in the cited bootstrap path.

semantic_findings.title: Bearer token can be sent to a caller-selected origin
semantic_findings.description: The CLI accepts a configurable service URL and sends the saved API key as a Bearer token in requests. An untrusted URL setting can therefore redirect credentials to another origin.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cited configuration and authenticated request code establish the credential flow. Exploitation depends on an attacker influencing the URL setting or command environment.

semantic_findings.title: Repository binding can retarget destructive publishing
semantic_findings.description: A project-local .revdoku file supplies a bucket identifier, and publication requests delete missing files. Publishing an untrusted checkout can therefore modify or remove content in a bucket accessible to the user.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The local binding is read without an interactive target confirmation, and the cited publish payload requests deletion of absent files. Exploitation requires valid credentials and a user-initiated publish.

semantic_findings.title: Existing credentials file permissions are not repaired
semantic_findings.description: Saving an API key sets a restrictive umask but does not explicitly chmod an existing credentials file. A previously permissive file can retain its permissions after being overwritten with a new key.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cited save routine establishes umask but lacks a permission repair step. The exposure requires an existing file with insecure mode on a shared system.

content.user_title: Publish Static Sites with Review Previews
content.value_statement: Publishing a static site can require separate tools for drafts, previews, and live releases. Revdoku manages local folders, private drafts, review links, and publication through one workflow.
actual_capabilities: Create a starter static site in a local folder.
Upload a local folder, file, or static SPA to a Revdoku bucket.
Create private drafts and temporary noindex review previews.
Publish a reviewed site with public, password, or email-gated access.
Store a project-local bucket binding for repeat deployments.
Open a published site or Revdoku dashboard from the CLI.
limitations: Requires a Revdoku account and authentication for remote operations.
Uploads only the files selected from the local path.
Public publishing is an external action and needs explicit approval.
The bundled installer currently downloads executable code without release-artifact verification.

use_cases.title: Review a marketing site before release
use_cases.description: Create a private draft and share a temporary review preview before a public launch.

use_cases.title: Deploy a static project folder
use_cases.description: Upload a finished HTML, CSS, JavaScript, or SPA folder and publish it after review.

use_cases.title: Share a protected client deliverable
use_cases.description: Publish a static deliverable with password or email-gated access for a limited audience.

prompt_templates.title: Create a first draft
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a simple static landing page in a new folder. Prepare it as a private Revdoku draft, not a public website.

prompt_templates.title: Request a review preview
prompt_templates.prompt: Upload the site in ./website as a private draft. Create a temporary noindex preview link and show me the URL.

prompt_templates.title: Publish after confirmation
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the files in ./dist. Explain what will be published, then ask for my confirmation before publishing it publicly.

prompt_templates.title: Update a protected site safely
prompt_templates.prompt: Check the Revdoku binding in this project. Show the target and changed files. After I confirm, update the existing password-protected website.

output_examples.input: Create a review preview for my site folder.
output: Private draft created from the selected folder.
Temporary noindex preview link is ready for review.
Target website and access mode are shown for confirmation.
After approval, the site is published and the live URL is provided.

best_practices: Create a private draft or preview before every public release.
Review the resolved bucket and changed files before approving publication.
Keep secrets outside the upload folder and verify exclusions before deployment.
anti_patterns: Do not publish an unreviewed folder from an untrusted repository.
Do not pass an untrusted service URL when using saved credentials.
Do not use the curl-to-bash installer until the downloaded artifact is verified.

faq.question: What can Revdoku publish?
faq.answer: It can publish static files, folders, and single-page applications from a local path.

faq.question: Can I review a site before it is public?
faq.answer: Yes. Create a private draft and use a temporary noindex preview link.

faq.question: Does publishing require confirmation?
faq.answer: It should. Publishing makes content externally available, so confirm the target and access mode first.

faq.question: How are repeat deployments targeted?
faq.answer: The CLI can store a project-local .revdoku binding with the target bucket details.

faq.question: Can I protect a published site?
faq.answer: Yes. The documented workflow supports password-protected and email-gated publication modes.

faq.question: What should I avoid uploading?
faq.answer: Keep credentials, private keys, environment files, and unrelated local data outside the selected upload folder.
